fast-signs.description: If you observe any of these symptoms in yourself or someone else, call the emergency stroke helpline immediately.

items.title: Face Drooping
items.text: Does one side of the face droop or is it numb? Ask the person to smile. Is the smile uneven?

items.title: Arm Weakness
items.text: Is one arm weak or numb? Ask the person to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?

items.title: Speech Difficulty
items.text: Is speech slurred? Is the person unable to speak or hard to understand? Ask them to repeat a simple sentence.

items.title: Time to Call Help
items.text: If the person shows any of these signs, even if the symptoms go away, check the time and call us immediately.

intro.label: Main Body Section
intro.title: What is Epilepsy?
intro.text:
Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent, unprovoked seizures. It affects over 50 million people worldwide, making it one of the most common neurological conditions. While epilepsy can develop at any age, it often begins in childhood or after age 60.

At our clinic, we understand that living with epilepsy affects every aspect of your life—from daily activities to personal relationships. Our comprehensive approach focuses not just on controlling seizures, but on improving your overall quality of life through evidence-based treatments and compassionate care.

types.label: Types of Seizures
types.title: Types of Seizures
types.description: Understanding the different types of seizures is crucial for proper diagnosis and treatment. Seizures are categorized based on where they begin in the brain.

items.title: Focal Onset Seizures
items.text: Begin in one area of the brain. May cause changes in sensation, emotions, or movements while the person remains conscious (focal aware) or may cause loss of awareness (focal impaired awareness).

items.title: Generalized Onset Seizures
items.text: Affect both sides of the brain simultaneously from the start. These include absence seizures (brief loss of awareness), tonic seizures (muscle stiffening), and clonic seizures (rhythmic jerking).

items.title: Unknown Onset Seizures
items.text: When the beginning of a seizure cannot be determined as focal or generalized. Further testing and monitoring may be needed to classify the seizure type accurately.

intro.title: What is a Headache Disorder?
intro.text:
A headache is pain or discomfort in the head or face area. While almost everyone experiences headaches occasionally, recurrent or persistent headaches can indicate an underlying disorder that requires expert medical evaluation and management.

Living with frequent headaches can significantly impact your work, relationships, and emotional well-being. Our clinic focuses on identifying your specific headache type and triggers, creating a customized plan combining preventive strategies and advanced treatments.

types.title: Common Headache Types
types.description: Headaches are classified as primary (not caused by another condition) or secondary (caused by an underlying health problem).

items.title: Tension Headache
items.text: The most common type, causing a constant dull ache or feeling of tight band pressure around the forehead, back of the head, and neck. Usually related to stress or muscle tension.

items.title: Cluster Headache
items.text: Severe, piercing pain that occurs in cycles or clusters, usually concentrated around one eye. Often accompanied by watering of the eye, nasal congestion, and restlessness.

items.title: Secondary Headache
items.text: Headaches resulting from other medical conditions, such as sinus infections, dental problems, high blood pressure, head injuries, or blood vessel issues in the brain.

intro.title: What is a Migraine?
intro.text:
A migraine is a neurological condition that causes intense, throbbing head pain, usually on one side. Unlike common tension headaches, migraines often present with associated symptoms like severe nausea, vomiting, and extreme sensitivity to light, sound, and smell.

An attack can last from several hours to days, making daily activities impossible. Our targeted diagnostic and therapy framework aims to reduce the severity and frequency of your migraine episodes using cutting-edge medical treatments.

items.title: Chronic Migraine

intro.title: What is a Movement Disorder?
intro.text:
Movement disorders are neurological conditions that affect the speed, fluency, quality, and ease of movement. They are typically divided into hyperkinetic disorders (causing excessive, involuntary movements, such as tremors or spasms) and hypokinetic disorders (causing slow, stiff, or reduced movements).

Involuntary movements or balance issues can make eating, writing, or walking extremely difficult. Our comprehensive diagnostic approach identifies the specific nerve or brain center origin to customize targeted medication regimens and therapy programs.

intro.title: What is Multiple Sclerosis?
intro.text:
Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, autoimmune disease of the central nervous system. In MS, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks myelin, the protective fatty sheath that covers nerve fibers in the brain and spinal cord. This causes inflammation and scarring (plaques), disrupting electrical signals.

Symptoms can vary from temporary numbness to difficulty walking or visual impairments. While there is no cure, today's Disease-Modifying Therapies (DMTs) can suppress immune activity, significantly reducing relapse rates and slowing disability progression.

items.title: Primary Progressive MS (PPMS)
items.text: Steady worsening of symptoms from the onset without distinct relapses or remissions. Typically diagnosed in patients after age 40.

items.title: Secondary Progressive (SPMS)

intro.title: What is Peripheral Neuropathy?
intro.text:
Peripheral neuropathy refers to damage or dysfunction of the peripheral nerves, which carry information between the brain, spinal cord, and the rest of the body. This condition often results in numbness, tingling, weakness, or sharp, burning pain, commonly starting in the feet and hands (known as a "stocking-glove" pattern).

Nerve damage can stem from diabetes, metabolic disorders, vitamin deficiencies, autoimmune diseases, or toxin exposures. Our clinical team focuses on identifying the root cause to halt nerve decline, relieve painful symptoms, and restore normal sensation.

intro.title: What is Parkinson's Disease?
intro.text:
Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that mainly affects dopamine-producing neurons in a specific area of the brain called the substantia nigra. Symptoms develop gradually over years, slowly impacting motor control, balance, and coordination.

Although Parkinson's cannot be cured completely, modern pharmaceutical management and surgical interventions like Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) can dramatically reduce symptoms and improve the patient's daily quality of life.

intro.title: What is Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation?
intro.text:
rTMS is a state-of-the-art neurological neuromodulation therapy. Unlike systemic medications, which affect the entire body, rTMS targets specific areas of the brain to stimulate neurons and restore healthy communication pathways.

An electromagnetic coil is placed gently against the patient's scalp. It delivers brief, highly focused magnetic pulses that stimulate nerve cells safely. The procedure is entirely painless, and patients remain awake and active throughout.

intro.title: What is a Stroke?
intro.text:
A stroke occurs when blood flow to an area of the brain is interrupted or reduced. This deprives brain cells of vital oxygen and nutrients, causing them to begin dying within minutes. A stroke is a critical emergency where rapid medical intervention can mean the difference between recovery and permanent disability.

Dr. Praveen Gupta is a pioneer in hyperacute stroke management in India, offering rapid thrombolytic therapies and mechanical thrombectomy. Beyond emergency care, our clinic specializes in stroke prevention and customized long-term neuro-rehabilitation.

items.text: Known as a "mini-stroke." Blood flow is blocked temporarily (often resolving within minutes). Although symptoms fade quickly, a TIA is a warning sign of an impending major stroke.

intro.title: What is Vertigo?
intro.text:
Vertigo is a sensation of spinning or motion when you are perfectly still. Often described as dizziness, it makes you feel as if your surroundings are moving. Vertigo is typically a symptom of an underlying vestibular system issue in the inner ear or brain.

Living with recurrent vertigo can lead to fall risks, anxiety, and extreme nausea. Our clinic focuses on accurate diagnosis, pinpointing peripheral or central causes, and utilizing drug-free therapies to resolve balance issues successfully.

items.title: Balance System
items.text: Linked to inner ear & brain

items.title: Often Drug-Free
items.text: Relieved by body maneuvers

items.title: Common Causes
items.text: BPPV is the main culprit

items.title: Therapeutic Rehab
items.text: Vestibular retraining works

types.label: Common Vertigo Types
types.title: Common Vertigo Types
types.description: Vertigo is categorized based on whether the origin is inside the inner ear balance canals or the brain.

items.title: BPPV
items.text: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo. Triggered by specific head movements, caused by tiny calcium carbonate crystals displacing into the inner ear fluid canals.

items.title: Peripheral Vertigo
items.text: Originates in the inner ear balance nerves. Common causes include vestibular neuritis (viral infection of the nerve) and Meniere's disease (fluid build-up in the ear).

items.title: Central Vertigo
items.text: Originates in the brainstem or cerebellum. Triggered by conditions like vestibular migraines, strokes, tumors, or multiple sclerosis.

warning.title: When to Seek Emergency Care
warning.description: Seek immediate medical attention if vertigo is accompanied by:

items.text: Double vision or blurred vision
Slurred speech or difficulty talking
Weakness or numbness in arms or legs
Difficulty walking or loss of coordination

symptoms.title: Vertigo Symptoms
symptoms.description: Vertigo presents with a spinning sensation that can trigger physical and sensory reflexes in the body.
symptoms.note_text: Symptoms are typically exacerbated by head movements, rolling over in bed, tilting the head upward, or sudden posture shifts.

diagnosis.label: Diagnosing Vertigo
diagnosis.title: Diagnosing Vertigo
diagnosis.description: Diagnosing vertigo involves checking both your balance systems and inner ear fluid pathways to identify positional triggers.

items.title: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver
items.text: A clinical movement test to trigger positional nystagmus (involuntary eye movement) and verify BPPV in the canals.

items.title: Vestibular Testing
items.text: Video-nystagmography (VNG) tests and caloric stimulation check inner ear balance responses.

items.title: Brain MRI
items.text: High-resolution imaging to rule out brainstem strokes, multiple sclerosis plaques, acoustic neuromas, or tumors.

items.title: Hearing Evaluation
items.text: Audiometry screening to rule out Meniere's disease or acoustic nerve issues that affect hearing pathways.

treatments.label: Treatment Options
treatments.title: Comprehensive Vertigo Treatment Options
treatments.description: Many types of vertigo can be resolved without pills. We offer targeted maneuvers and custom physical rehabilitation therapies.

items.title: Canalith Repositioning (Epley Maneuver)
items.subtitle: Drug-free physical crystal resetting
items.text: For BPPV sufferers, a series of structured head movements guided by the doctor rolls floating ear crystals back into place, providing relief.

items.title: Vestibular Rehabilitation Therapy (VRT)
items.subtitle: Retraining balance & stabilizing gaze
items.text: Custom exercises designed to help your brain compensate for inner ear abnormalities, improving stability and reducing fall risk.

items.title: Pharmacological Therapies
items.subtitle: Vestibular suppressants & anti-emetics
items.text: Medications can help control severe acute symptoms of dizziness and nausea during flare-ups or viral infections of the vestibular nerve.

items.title: Diet & Safety Guidance
items.subtitle: Low-sodium dietary support & safety checks
items.text: For Meniere's disease, dietary fluid control (limiting salt and caffeine) helps manage pressure build-up in the inner ear canals.
